item.title: Hidden for 7,000 years: the enigmatic skeleton from Großköllnbach
item.description: Twisted body, striking neck vertebrae, unusual burial: a Neolithic skeleton found in Lower Bavaria puzzles experts. Who was the young person buried in a pit 7,000 years ago, and why was the body placed there so strangely?

item.title: Thousands of supermarket fridges still exposed after cyberattack
item.description: No group has claimed the attack, and experts warn thousands of similarly exposed devices remain online as a separate incident disrupts Dutch grocer Albert Heijn.

item.title: Mont Blanc rises by almost two metres, now standing at 4,807.47 metres
item.description: An altitude that "is close to the historical value" measured at the end of the 19th century, but still not enough to draw conclusions about the effects of global warming.

item.title: One person killed and 20 others injured in overnight Russian attacks on Kyiv
item.description: Ukrainian authorities say some of the Russian strikes targeted energy infrastructures, a few days after US President Donald Trump announced an "energy ceasefire".

item.title: Mont Blanc: new French measurements, summit 'grows' to 4,807m
item.description: New measurements from Saint-Gervais-Mont-Blanc show Western Europe's highest peak at 4,807.47 metres, almost two metres higher than in 2023. Experts say the change is due to the thickness of the snow and ice cap.

item.title: FBI arrest Saudi OpenAI employee for allegedly planting recording device in office
item.description: The ex-OpenAI employee allegedly wrapped a USB device in toilet paper and inserted it into a television located in an "executive conference room".

item.title: Croatia's wartime grievances threaten Montenegro's hopes of joining EU by 2028
item.description: Croatia's list of grievances with Montenegro include missing persons, war crimes, prison camps, property seizures and borders. Podgorica has closed 21 of 33 chapters, but Zagreb is blocking progress unless bilateral issues are resolved.

item.title: Todd Haynes at Lumière Festival: 'It is a time to remember how important it is to protect our freedoms'
item.description: "It is a time to remember how important it is to protect our freedoms, and our ability to speak freely." Euronews Culture sits down with celebrated filmmaker Todd Haynes during this year's Lumière Film Festival.

item.title: Turkish police raid Halk TV in Istanbul, sparking outrage over media freedom
item.description: Police barricades surrounded the headquarters of Halk TV in Istanbul on Wednesday, 14 October, as Turkish authorities raided the independent broadcaster and appointed a trustee to take control of its operations.

item.title: Spanish Foreign Minister tells Euronews 'fundamental rights of people' at stake in snap election
item.description: Albares says upcoming election pits 'progressive majority' against rightwing forces that want to remove fundamental rights. He also discusses Madrid's position ahead of an EU leaders summit on Thursday, advocating to use Russian frozen assets to finance Ukraine

item.title: EU summit: Leaders tackle energy prices, spar over budget and unite on Ukraine
item.description: The two-day summit of EU leaders comes with a packed agenda topped by energy prices, the long-term budget and Russia's war on Ukraine. Hybrid warfare, enlargement and migration will also feature prominently.

item.title: Rutte urges allies to send more air defence to Ukraine
item.description: NATO Secretary General, Mark Rutte said allies need to do more to support Ukraine, especially in air defences. His pleas come amid drastic Russian escalation over the skies in Kyiv.

item.title: Louvre could be forced to close without major overhaul, director warns
item.description: A year after thieves made off with €88 million of crown jewels that have never been found, the new man in charge says leaking pipes and crumbling galleries mean security fixes alone won’t save the Paris landmark.

item.title: Russia’s internet shutdowns push state firms back to landline phones
item.description: State procurement of landline telephones tripled in the first eight months of 2026 as mobile internet outages hit nearly 80% of the country. Rostelecom’s chief urged Russians to keep one at home “like a fire extinguisher".

item.title: Entire Swedish reality show season lost weeks before premiere amid disputed AI claims
item.description: The project could not be restored, wiping out hundreds of days of work, according to Swedish newspaper Aftonbladet.

item.title: Germany: Supporters rally in Hamburg as trial opens over Nord Stream pipeline blasts
item.description: Supporters waving Ukrainian flags gathered outside a court in Hamburg on Wednesday, 14 October, in solidarity with a former Ukrainian army officer accused of involvement in the 2022 Nord Stream pipeline explosions in the Baltic Sea.

item.title: Holidays remain a ‘spending priority’, but ‘cost-conscious’ travel is on the rise, report reveals
item.description: Travellers are planning on booking cheaper accommodation and eating out less while away, rather than giving up holidays completely.

item.title: Major artworks by masters on sale as Monsoon's Peter Simon clears out collection
item.description: Assembled over decades, the art owned by Peter Simon, founder of the Monsoon fashion store, is one of Britain's foremost collections of modern and contemporary art.

item.title: US inflation rises to 3.7% as fuel costs climb ahead of midterms
item.description: Higher petrol prices and airfares pushed US inflation to 3.7% in September, adding pressure on households and the Federal Reserve weeks before the midterm elections.

item.title: Meet the 76-year-old Kazakh traveller on a mission to walk around the world
item.description: Sarsenbay Kotyrashov began travelling on foot in his 70s. After walking across Kazakhstan and through parts of Asia and Europe, he is now preparing to cross the US.

item.title: Exploring Dubrovnik: Lilly’s epic Adriatic adventure of history and thrills
item.description: Dubrovnik welcomes more than a million visitors a year. Join Lilly Douse as she explores its historic Old Town, tries traditional Croatian cooking, and heads out onto the Adriatic Sea.

item.title: Kazakhstan seeks Antwerp-Bruges partnership to boost trade via Middle Corridor
item.description: Kazakhstan is seeking closer cooperation with Belgium on the Middle Corridor, including a potential partnership between the Port of Antwerp-Bruges and the Caspian ports of Aktau and Kuryk, as King Philippe and Queen Mathilde make their first state visit to the country.

item.title: Lufthansa beats Air France-KLM to €1.2bn stake in TAP Air Portugal
item.description: Portugal has chosen Lufthansa to buy a 44.9% stake in TAP, completing the first phase of the airline’s privatisation. The deal still needs regulatory approval.

item.title: World’s oldest shipwreck off Turkey: 4,700-year-old amphorae discovered
item.description: The shipwreck found near Antalya’s Kekova Island, dated to roughly 4,400–4,700 years ago, sheds light on maritime trade in the eastern Mediterranean.

item.title: French journalist Natacha Polony joins growing field of 2027 presidential hopefuls
item.description: She is stepping away from her role as an observer to make herself "useful" to her country, denouncing a France mired in "chaos", amid a debt crisis, "tragic" unrest in secondary schools and a "total lack of prospects."

item.title: IEA warns diesel prices in Europe could rise as global crunch lasts into 2027
item.description: Europe could face renewed wholesale diesel price rises in the coming weeks, the International Energy Agency warned on Wednesday, as disrupted supplies leave markets tight well into 2027 despite recovering Gulf oil output.

item.title: ‘Heartbreaking’ elephants and wily coyotes: Wildlife Photographer of the Year 2026 – in pictures
item.description: This year's winners showcase powerful stories from the natural world and the urgent need to protect it.

item.title: Tsui Hark at Lumière Festival: ‘We don't know where the future will bring us’
item.description: "We all know that the thing about humanity is that we always fear being replaced by something." Euronews Culture sits down with legendary Hong Kong filmmaker Tsui Hark during this year's Lumière Film Festival.

item.title: Japan summons Russian ambassador to protest journalist's arrest on spying charges
item.description: Moscow's FSB security service said a Japanese national was arrested on the Far East island of Sakhalin, near a disputed cluster of islands, but did not name the individual.

item.title: Prosecution calls Russell Brand 'ruthless' sexual predator at opening of sex assault trial
item.description: Brand is on bail and arrived at court Wednesday to a crowed of photographers and video journalists. He said he felt "blessed."

item.title: MEPs urge EU to shield International Criminal Court from US sanctions
item.description: Lawmakers from across the political spectrum say the EU should activate the Blocking Statute to prevent European companies from complying with measures imposed by the US administration, defined as an "attack by a foreign power."

item.title: How Germany is training medical staff to fight Ebola
item.description: With 9,000 infections and 4,000 deaths, Ebola continues to spread in eastern DR Congo. German experts are training local healthcare workers to treat patients safely and contain the virus.

item.title: EU's methane rules face one-year delay, sparking environmental backlash
item.description: Environmentalists warn that delaying EU methane rules will do little to lower energy prices, accusing Brussels of using energy security and competitiveness to justify weakening the Green Deal.

item.title: Climate change is putting Europe’s brain health at risk
item.description: Rising temperatures, poor air quality and the spread of infectious diseases could increase the burden of neurological disorders, with the most vulnerable communities facing the greatest risks.

item.title: Latest news bulletin | October 14th, 2026 – Midday
item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this October 14th, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: A new night train will launch between Hamburg and Munich in March 2027
item.description: Nox Mobility’s first night train will link Hamburg and Munich via Bremen and Augsburg, with individual private ‘suites’ for all passengers.

item.title: Portuguese parliament backs extension of parental leave: what changes?
item.description: The new legal framework, arising from a joint proposal by PS and PSD, will give parents a more favourable regime than the one currently in force.

item.title: Iran executes man accused of armed attacks during US-Israeli strikes
item.description: Ali-Sina Mostafavi, 38, a mountaineer and musician from Kerman, was executed on charges of “enmity against God” after being accused of firing on civilians and soldiers during the opening months of the war. He was also charged with participating in the January protests and sending footage

item.title: Former Ukrainian military officer to stand trial in Germany over Nord Stream sabotage
item.description: While some in the West were quick to accuse Russia of sabotaging its own gas export route, German investigators identified a cell of Ukrainians they say were the alleged perpetrators.

item.title: As the US and China race ahead in AI, France carves its own path with Nvidia’s help
item.description: Nvidia bets almost $10 billion in Europe as Paris pushes for AI sovereignty.

item.title: Albania: Student protests in Tirana turn violent as Flamingo Revolution escalates
item.description: Albania's capital, Tirana, saw violent clashes between student protesters and police on Tuesday, 13 October, as demonstrations continued overnight into Wednesday.

item.title: Duane Davis gets minimum 40 years in prison for orchestrating murder of Tupac Shakur
item.description: Shakur was a key figure in a hip-hop rivalry pitting the US East Coast against the West Coast. He was just 25 when he was gunned down in Las Vegas.

item.title: These are the best holiday destinations in Europe for embracing a longevity lifestyle
item.description: Put down the red light masks in favour of walking more, socialising over a glass of wine and eating plant-based food at these longevity hot spots on the continent.

item.title: ASML posts record €11.7 billion in sales but warns it can’t keep up with AI demand
item.description: Dutch equipment supplier ASML warned on Wednesday that its planned supply of machines will not fully meet customers’ AI-driven demand in 2027 and 2028, as it reported record quarterly sales of around €11.7 billion and lifted the lower end of its full-year sales forecast.

item.title: Retro trend: is China simply copying the German VW Beetle here?
item.description: Citroën's 2CV has just been unveiled as an electric car, and the retro Fiat 500 is already a hit. Few know that in China even Germany's VW Beetle is making a comeback, but only in looks.

item.title: Trump faces backlash after posting 'sick' video of UK man killed by tiger
item.description: The man in the real video, identified by the BBC as William Chapman, later died from his injuries following the Saturday incident, police said.

item.title: EU’s AI rules face first enforcement test over lab incidents
item.description: The EU is investigating OpenAI and Anthropic over AI agents that hacked outside organisations, raising questions about whether the AI Act covers rogue models escaping the testing environment.

item.title: Africa records world's fastest gains in disaster resilience, new study shows
item.description: The World Risk Poll, which surveyed 143,000 people across 140 countries, found North Africa up five points and Southern Africa up four, driven by expanding internet access and household preparedness. Yet 220 million people affected by disasters in the past five years received no warning.

item.title: World’s oldest shipwreck discovered off Turkey’s Mediterranean coast
item.description: Archaeologists say a 4,400- to 4,700-year-old shipwreck found near Kekova Island in southern Turkey carried ceramic storage pots and stone anchors across the Mediterranean.

item.title: Storm chaos in Santiago as hail, floods and power cuts slam Chile’s capital
item.description: Heavy rain, hail and thunderstorms flooded Santiago, Chile, on Tuesday, 13 October, disrupting transport and leaving over 36,000 electricity customers without power. Chile’s disaster agency, Senapred, declared a red alert across the Metropolitan Region.
